# `silk/i8`

<!-- Generated by packages/compiler/scripts/generate-documentation.mjs. Do not edit by hand. -->

Eight-bit signed integers for compact values, byte-level formats, and narrow arithmetic.

## When to use

Use `i8` when an external format or data structure requires exactly eight signed bits. Prefer a
wider integer for general arithmetic: the small range makes accidental overflow easy.

## Details

Ordinary arithmetic, narrowing conversions, division by zero, and invalid shift counts trap.
Choose `checked*` when failure is data, `wrapping*` for arithmetic modulo 2^8, or `saturating*`
when results should clamp to [`MIN`](#declaration-73696c6b2f69383a3a4d494e) or [`MAX`](#declaration-73696c6b2f69383a3a4d4158). Signed right shifts preserve the sign bit.

Decimal [`parse`](#declaration-73696c6b2f69383a3a7061727365) consumes the complete input and distinguishes malformed text from a value
outside the i8 range. [`toText`](#declaration-73696c6b2f69383a3a746f54657874) allocates an owned decimal string.

## Gotchas

[`MIN`](#declaration-73696c6b2f69383a3a4d494e) has no positive i8 counterpart, so ordinary [`negate`](#declaration-73696c6b2f69383a3a6e6567617465) traps for that one value.

Import as `i8` with `import silk.i8`.

Public declarations: 60.

<a id="declaration-73696c6b2f69383a3a4d4158"></a>
